name: Switching induces a second current
summary: Faraday found that switching a current on or off in one coil on an iron ring briefly drives a current in a second, separate coil: electromagnetic induction.
description: Separately insulated windings around an iron ring connect to a battery and a remote galvanometer. Making or breaking the battery circuit gives opposite transient responses; steady current gives no sustained deflection.
tier_reason: Induction is a reusable physical principle behind transformers and electrical engineering across generations; the experiment is its bounded witness.
why: After Ørsted showed in 1820 that electricity produces magnetism, Faraday spent years looking for the reverse effect.

events.caveats: This is an experimental result, not the later mathematical flux law or an efficient power transformer. The report deliberately rearranged experiments for exposition.
